pr_title: sqlite,test,doc: accept Buffer and URL as paths
pr_body:
Closes #56940

This PR adds the capability to the sqlite module to accept Buffer and URL as the database location.

I think this needs a rebase to fix the CI issue.

cc: @nodejs/sqlite since this PR was opened before the team existed.

> Maybe it's because I'm used to using better-sqlite3.
> 
> This library allows you to serialize a sqlite database in the form of a buffer. It also lets you create an in-memory database from a buffer.
> 
> So I'm wondering whether it's appropriate to allow a buffer to be used as a file path to initialize a sqlite db, rather than using it as a sqlite db binary.
> 
> Refs: https://github.com/WiseLibs/better-sqlite3/blob/master/docs/api.md#new-databasepath-options
> 
> > In-memory databases can also be created by passing a buffer returned by [.serialize()](https://github.com/WiseLibs/better-sqlite3/blob/master/docs/api.md#serializeoptions---buffer), instead of passing a string as the first argument.

Very interesting.

This PR is about making `node:sqlite` consistent with other modules that deal with `path`.

 It would reduce compatibility with better-sqlite3 but I think it is worth it. In the backup implementation, we took a different path than better-sqlite3 too.

I don't know what other people think.
We can always support the better-sqlite3 functionality (in a different PR) by making the serialized database buffer an option instead of the path argument.

issue_context.title: Make sqlite module consitent with other modules like fs
issue_context.body:
### What is the problem this feature will solve?

`node:sqlite` module deals with paths for the database location. We should support `Buffer` and `URL` following up on [this comment](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/56253#discussion_r1928924403). Just like [fs](https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html#fspromisesopenpath-flags-mode) does.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Support both the three options: String, Buffer and URL

### What alternatives have you considered?

_No response_
comments: I will work on it before the aggregate function 😃

review_comments:
You should also check the happy path.

Can you try `URL("file://path/to/db.db?mode=ro")` and verify that writes error out?

Passing a `file://` or `file:` as URL as a string or Buffer should also be supported.

We should also check if a string or Buffer based `file://` URI works.

Also check `file:/path/to/db`.
It has landed already. Do you want to add it (in a new PR?).
